facts.raw_span: decreased vision in her right eye
Symptoms began 4 days prior to presentation
struck by lightning directly to the right forehead
Uncorrected visual acuity measured 20/50 OD and 20/20 OS
Pupils were symmetric, with no relative afferent pupillary defect
Initial anterior segment examination was normal with absence of cataract
Initial dilated fundus examination showed no apparent abnormalities in either eye
central macular thickening in fundus examination at 2 weeks
mild posterior subcapsular cataract visible in right eye at 7 weeks
Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption in the right eye at two weeks post-injury
Restoration of foveal contour with decreased cystoid abnormalities, small subfoveal hyporeflective space, and further loss of outer retinal layers in the nasal macula at seven weeks post-injury
Persistent subfoveal hyporeflective space in the inner retina with interval restoration of subfoveal outer retinal structures at four months post-injury

concepts.why: The patient was struck by lightning and later developed a cataract, which is a known complication of lightning strikes.
The patient was struck by lightning and later developed macular thickening, cystoid changes, and ellipsoid zone disruption, which are consistent with lightning-induced maculopathy.

rationales.F03: The patient was directly struck by lightning, which is a known cause of both cataract and maculopathy.
rationales.F06: The absence of cataract in the initial examination makes it less likely that the patient had a pre-existing cataract.
rationales.F09: The development of a posterior subcapsular cataract is consistent with lightning-induced cataract.
rationales.F10: Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption are characteristic of maculopathy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's decreased vision, central macular thickening, and intraretinal cystoid changes are more directly explained by lightning-induced maculopathy, despite the development of a cataract.
